source.title: When Forgotten Facts Return: Relearning-Aware Unlearning of Knowledge Graph Embeddings via Tangent Kernels
source.authors: Parnian Fazel; Mohammad M Maheri; Hamed Haddadi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures recovery under continued training after knowledge-graph unlearning, extending benign-relearning evaluation to knowledge-graph embeddings rather than LLMs. It also evaluates a proposed counter-method in that setting.
record.gate_note: The study tests ordinary continued training on retained and never-trained graph edges, with a retrained oracle receiving the same update. It does not test fine-tuning on a small set of examples, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-based attacks. Reported literature results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests benign relearning in a new setting: knowledge-graph embeddings (TransE, TransH, RotatE on FB15k-237 and CoDEx-L), not LLMs. The update is ordinary continued training on retained and never-trained edges and contains no forgotten fact. Leakage is measured as the rise in forget-set MRR beyond a retrained oracle given the identical update. GraphDPO and ZeroFisher forget to near-oracle level at release, then recover beyond the oracle, which bears on A and B. The study also tests counter-methods: its own KAU, NTK/SAM/TAR add-ons on GraphDPO, and substituted robust objectives such as SAM variants, TAR-style, Booster and NTK scrubbing. These bear on F. Reader codes V1/V2/V6 map to A/B/F.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that KG unlearners GraphDPO and ZeroFisher, though near the retrained oracle at release, let forgotten facts return beyond the oracle under ordinary continued training, through shared entity embeddings. KAU substantially reduces that leakage (46–82%) at higher retained utility, though not to zero. They add that existing relearning defences (NTK, SAM, TAR, and substituted objectives) do not close the gap.
record.recipe_differences: This study tests knowledge-graph embedding unlearning and benign continued training, not the named LLM unlearning recipes or their prompting, ablation and quantization attacks. It compares GraphDPO and ZeroFisher with the proposed tangent-kernel method KAU.
record.method_sensitivity: Leakage is reported across dataset and backbone, and across update-data configurations. The study reports a separate never-trained-edges-only update, and comparisons at different forgetting depths. The add-on and ablation results also vary with the unlearning objective or component.

fits_no_version.finding: Hybrid-model attribution: the involved entity rows carry 91–105% of the forget-MRR rise, relation rows at most 5.4% for unlearners. The retrained oracle also recovers through the same rows (Table 14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign relearning after embedding unlearning flows through parameters shared between forgotten and update facts.

record.problems: The experiments concern knowledge-graph embeddings, not LLMs. The reported update is a fixed family of graph-training configurations and does not cover the claim's prompting, quantization or activation-ablation attacks. Main results use seven unlearning seeds; add-on and ablation comparisons use three seeds. Some selected results are reported at method-specific highest-leakage configurations.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant reported recovery result was omitted from the extracted rows. Other appendix measurements, such as parameter-block hybrid attribution and response-ranking correlations, were not included because they do not directly measure leakage recovery as specified by versions A, B or F.

untested.parts: LLMs; near-chance target accuracy (the reference is a retrained oracle); prompting, quantization and ablation attacks.
LLM fine-tuning; relearning on a subset of the forgotten facts; truly unrelated data (the update edges share entities with forgotten facts).
Not tested: no activation-direction ablation and no access-vs-deletion probing analysis.
Resistance to prompting, quantization or ablation attacks; LLM settings.

missing.what: Release-time forget/retain/test MRR showing GraphDPO/ZeroFisher forget to near-oracle level before recovery (e.g. TransE MF 0.2301 vs gold 0.2211, original 0.2733). This is needed for A's 'works at release' premise.
Leakage across all 48 update configurations: flat along every axis, and KAU lowest in every configuration (TransE).
Oracle retraining-seed check: every method's rise exceeds the oracle's at all three oracle seeds; KAU leak is 5–7.7x the oracle seed SD.
Leakage vs forgetting depth: baselines' RER grows over twice as fast with depth as KAU's.
40-epoch update changes leakage little (KAU 0.0217, GraphDPO 0.0412, ZeroFisher 0.0697).

record.verdict_notes: The setting is knowledge-graph embeddings, not LLMs, so all verdicts apply only to that setting (T3). Reader codes V1/V2/V6 are remapped to A/B/F. Where a row links to two versions with opposite readings, the state given is for the first-named primary version and the problem text states the other. T4 rows are ablations of the study's own method and are unlinked; T4-NO-ANTICIPATION duplicates T5-PLAIN. The reader's B limits_scope label about the non-small update set was dropped: that is an untested part, not a limit. The update set is not small: the standard update has 40k edges, but the never-trained-only update (6,000 edges, about 2% of training) is closer to B. Results are reported at each method's highest-leakage configuration. T2/T4/T5 rows use 3 seeds.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test chance accuracy, LLM unlearning, or prompting, ablation and quantization attacks. It does test whether continued training recovers targeted knowledge after knowledge-graph unlearning.
The update is ordinary continued training on retained and never-trained graph edges; the study does not test small unrelated or loosely related fine-tuning sets, or a subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation is performed, and the analysis does not test whether LLM unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language or in-context prompting attack is tested.
KAU is evaluated against continued training on graph edges, not against prompt-based, quantization or activation-ablation attacks.
